links.comparator_used: Baseline LLM responses without grounding (model's own knowledge) versus a Wikipedia-grounded condition
links.outcome: Readability classification of LLM outputs across systems and metrics, in English and Portuguese
links.effect: 1,120 data points from seven systems, five readability metrics. Systems were statistically homogeneous at baseline but significantly heterogeneous under Wikipedia grounding. Metric variability was significant in all conditions. No overall direction of readability change or numeric effect size is given in the abstract.
links.tradeoff: Grounding on a verified source produced inconsistent readability across systems, so readability was not reliably preserved or improved. The metrics are not interchangeable, so the apparent effect depends on which metric is used.
links.quote: Although retrieval grounding is commonly used to improve accuracy, our findings show a trade-off: verified-source grounding can yield inconsistent readability.
